retryable_conditions: A transport-raised exception whose class name contains 'timeout' (case-insensitive) -- classified TIMEOUT.
HTTP 5xx -- classified PROVIDER_ERROR (retried the same as a rate limit/timeout, since a 5xx is transient-server-side by definition).
non_retryable_conditions: Any other 4xx (e.g. 401/403/404) fails immediately with zero retries -- an auth/permission/not-found error will not resolve by waiting.
retry_backoff_contract.partial_success_rule: If a later page's fetch fails after retries are exhausted, but the bars already sanitized from EARLIER successful pages already meet required_bars, the failure is ignored and the symbol is still reported READY -- a transient failure fetching MORE history than needed must not downgrade an already-sufficient result.

tests.test_timeout_then_successful_retry_reach: 1 timeout exception, then a successful page -> READY, retries=1, exactly one backoff sleep of 1.0s recorded via an injected sleep_fn (no real sleeping occurs in the test).
tests.test_timeout_retry_exhaustion_fails_clos: 4 consecutive timeout exceptions (1 initial + 3 retries, all failing) -> status TIMEOUT, retries=3, zero bars returned.
tests.test_rate_limit_then_success: One HTTP 429 then a successful page -> READY, retries=1.
tests.test_rate_limit_exhaustion_fails_closed: 4 consecutive HTTP 429 responses -> status RATE_LIMITED, retries=3.
tests.test_non_retryable_4xx_fails_immediately: A single HTTP 403 -> status PROVIDER_ERROR, retries=0, exactly one transport call made (no retry attempted).

pagination_evidence.test_multi_page_response_paginates_until: Two pages (80 bars each, linked via next_page_token) both fetched, combined bar_count=160 -> READY, pages_fetched=2, second request's params include page_token from the first response.
pagination_evidence.test_pagination_stops_once_sufficient_ev: A single page already meeting required_bars, WITH a next_page_token present in the response, does NOT trigger a second request -- pages_fetched=1. Bounded by both sufficiency and a hard max_pages=20 safety cap (never exercised in these tests, since no symbol needs 20 pages of 1-minute bars to reach 120).

isolation_evidence.test_one_symbol_alpaca_failure_isolated_: AAPL's transport call raises a timeout on every attempt (Alpaca fully fails for AAPL, and this fake's yfinance leg also gives 0 for AAPL, so AAPL ends not-ready); MSFT's own separate transport call succeeds normally and reaches READY in the same preseed_and_verify() batch call -- one bad symbol does not abort or affect any other symbol's fetch.

live_read_evidence.description: 35/35 real symbols against the live Alpaca PAPER data endpoint all returned on the FIRST page with zero retries (see readiness_by_symbol.csv) -- no rate limiting or timeout was encountered in this live check, which exercised the non-error, non-retry path against the real account/entitlement. Retry/rate-limit/timeout behavior itself is only exercisable deterministically via the mocked unit tests above (a real rate-limit or outage cannot be reliably triggered on demand against a live provider).
